::: {.header-box}
# Pesticide poisoning in South Africa

**11,690 cases · 1,500 deaths · R2.34 billion · per year.**

*Three coordinated policy actions retire most of it at ~R300k/year — no new legislation required.*
:::

## The problem in one line

::: {.key-stat}
**Detection is incomplete, the response loop is broken, and the worst single product is still freely registered.** Three problems → three briefs → one integrated system.
:::

## Three briefs, three asks

::: {.grid-2col}

::: {.option-summary}
### 1 · Detect — Surveillance ★
**Ask:** Adopt the Surveillance MVP — PIH dashboard/MVD (S1) + BChE auto-notify (S2). NHLS→NMC IT feed now operational.
**Cost:** R117,000/yr
**Impact:** Per-case detection 5 % → 19 % (almost 4×); enables faster, targeted response.
**Time:** 12 weeks
**Owner:** NICD · NHLS · PIH
:::

::: {.option-summary}
### 2 · Act — Coordination ★
**Ask:** Joint NDoH–DALRRD DG circular adopting the Coordination Full Package — closure-of-loop NMC field, structured DALRRD referral, NICD→DALRRD intelligence feed, clinician feedback, joint KPI dashboard.
**Cost:** R145,000/yr
**Impact:** P(loop closed) 1.1 % → ~70 %; ~957 deaths averted/yr at scale
**Time:** 12 weeks for MVP (C1+C3), 12 months for full package
**Owner:** NICD-led, DALRRD partner
:::

:::

::: {.grid-2col}

::: {.option-summary}
### 3 · Restrict — Terbufos ★
**Ask:** DALRRD adopt Option T2 (formulation restriction + RUP designation + distributor audit), with a hard-coded 24-month evaluation gate to Option T3 (full ban) if attributable serious cases do not fall by a pre-agreed margin.
**Cost:** ~R1–3M/yr DALRRD enforcement
**Impact:** Removes the dominant agent in fatal SA paediatric pesticide poisoning; leverage ratio ~1 : 500 on household mortality.
**Time:** Gazette T2 within 3 months; T3 decision at 24 months.
**Owner:** DALRRD Pesticide Registrar
:::

::: {.option-summary}
### How the three connect
**Detect** generates the evidence the **Act** loop needs.
The closed loop terminates in **Restrict** decisions (starting with terbufos).
Outcomes of those decisions feed back into the surveillance system.
**Each ask stands alone; together they are strictly more valuable.**
:::

:::

## Who bears the R2.34 billion

| Stakeholder | Annual burden borne | Share |
|:------------|---------------------:|------:|
| NDoH — public hospitals (UPFS ward + ICU + drugs) | ~R70M | 3.0 % |
| NHLS — laboratory (BChE + GC-MS + repeat chem) | ~R10M | 0.4 % |
| DALRRD — regulator | R0 (lever-holder) | 0 % |
| Individuals — OOP + lost wages | ~R10M | 0.4 % |
| Households / wider society — lost lifetime earnings | ~R2.25B | 96.2 % |
| **Total** | **R2.34B** | **100 %** |

: Audited decomposition. Mortality (~96 %) falls on households via lost lifetime earnings (25 productive yr × R60k median income, undiscounted). Health-sector share is modest in absolute terms but it is the only column on a departmental budget line. {.striped}

---

## The economics

::: {.recommendation-box}
### ~R300k of operating spend retires ~R1.5B of preventable burden

**Total annual operating cost (Detect + Act):** ~R300,000 (less than one additional epidemiologist's salary).
**Modelled burden avoided at scale:** ~R1.45 billion / year (Coordination Full Package; see [Coordination brief §6c](posts/coordination_policy.qmd#what-changes-under-each-coordination-scenario)).
**Stakeholder split of that avoided burden:** ~R50M to NDoH+NHLS budget lines; ~R1.4B to households.
**ROI:** ~1,000× on narrow surveillance cost; ~220× on whole-system cost.
**Legal basis:** NHA §90 + existing NMC regulations + Act 36 of 1947.
:::

---

## What we are *not* asking for

- No new legislation.
- No new test, no new reagent contract (S2 is an LIS configuration).
- No new agency.
- No single point-estimate masquerading as certainty — every figure traces back to [`amua_import_parameters_v3.csv`](amua_import_parameters_v3.csv); open evidence gaps are listed in the [Parameters Hub](parameters_hub.qmd).
